info.name: Withings (aifitnessapi.com)
info.description: Withings: OAuth 2.0 and Webhook samples requests built from the vendor documentation aifitnessapi.com quotes. Generated by scripts/build-collections.mjs; no secrets included. https://aifitnessapi.com/collections

item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Withings's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection. No refresh request: Withings says to call the same requesttoken service with the refresh token and always keep the new refresh token, but its snippet shows only the code exchange, so this tool prints no refresh command rather than guess its parameters.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/integrate/withings-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://account.withings.com/oauth2_user/authorize2. Authorization URL. Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Withings redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Withings developer guide, “Authorization URL”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/oauth-authorization-url/

Scope: Comma-separated, as in Withings' example URL. Source: Withings developer guide, “Authorization URL”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/oauth-authorization-url/

Documented scopes (joined with commas):
- user.info: Account information, linked devices, goals, and device linking; also needed to list and subscribe to user-related notifications
- user.metrics: Health measurements, heart recordings, stethoscope data and goals; also needed for notification management
- user.activity: Physical activity and sleep; also needed for notification management
- user.sleepevents: Notifications for sleep events (bed in, bed out, inflate done)

PKCE: Not mentioned on the Withings authorization or token pages.

https://wbsapi.withings.net/v2/oauth2. Token exchange: POST action=requesttoken to https://wbsapi.withings.net/v2/oauth2, with a nonce and a signature computed from your client secret (Withings' “Request Signature” page).

Source: Withings developer guide, “Access and refresh tokens”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/access-and-refresh-tokens-no-recover/

Withings signs this request: get a nonce from its signature service and compute the signature with your client secret as its “Request Signature” page describes, then put both in the nonce and signature variables. This collection does not compute them.

Token lifetime: Access token 3 hours; refresh token 1 year; the old refresh token lasts 8 hours after a new one is issued, or until the new access token is used. Source: Withings developer guide, “Access and refresh tokens”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/access-and-refresh-tokens-no-recover/

Note: The authorization code is valid for 30 seconds. Source: Withings developer guide, “Authorization URL”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/oauth-authorization-url/

Note: Refresh tokens rotate: replace the stored one every time. Source: Withings developer guide, “Access and refresh tokens”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/access-and-refresh-tokens-no-recover/

Note: mode=demo on the authorization URL logs in a demo user for testing. Source: Withings developer guide, “Authorization URL”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/oauth-authorization-url/

Note: The token request is signed: Withings' snippet adds a signature computed with the client secret. Source: Withings developer guide, “Access and refresh tokens”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/get-access/access-and-refresh-tokens-no-recover/

item.name: Webhook samples
item.description:
Withings's documented example notifications, sent to {{local_url}} (your local handler) unchanged. Signature: No body signature. Append a secret query parameter to the callback URL (Withings' example: ?token=<random-secret>) and check it, plus an allowlist of the IP ranges Withings publishes as DNS TXT records. Source: Withings developer guide, “Notifications overview”, https://developer.withings.com/developer-guide/v3/integration-guide/public-health-data-api/data-api/notifications/notification-overview/

Headers that carry a signature hold the placeholder Withings prints, so a handler that verifies signatures will reject these: to send correctly signed requests, use https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks/send-sample.mjs. Respond: An application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST; return HTTP 2xx within a few seconds, then fetch the data from the Data API.

Payload library with JSON Schemas: https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks#withings.
